commit.message:
osctld: prepare child descriptors before applying process limits

Applying a container's NOFILE limit while its forked helper is still
closing inherited descriptors can prevent opening /proc/self/fd. The
helper then exits before returning a wrapper PID, aborting that autostart
item with EOF instead of reaching the normal start result.

Require the child to acknowledge completed descriptor cleanup and setup
before the privileged parent applies the configured limits and releases
the workload. Close helper-owned pipes on failure and collect only the
failed helper PID, preserving caller ownership after a successful handoff.
Retain existing descriptor, Ruby IO owner and socket cleanup behavior.

Cover the ordering with a gated fork and actual low NOFILE limit, plus
failed handshakes and process cleanup. Add a packaged-helper VM regression
with excess inherited descriptors and parallel container autostart,
configured limits, console, exec and clean stop coverage.

This changes only the private helper handshake. Existing process limits,
container state and public interfaces remain compatible across nodes.

os: fix large-swap setup on current kernel lines

The proactive-swap identity bitmap needs one bit per swap page. Using a
kmalloc-only bitmap allocator requests an unsupported allocation order
for sufficiently large swap devices, so swapon fails despite free RAM.

Pin the repaired, folded downstream patches for Linux 6.12.113 and
6.18.49. They use kvcalloc with vmalloc fallback and pair both failure
cleanup and swapoff with kvfree. Keep both selected base versions, all
retained kernel entries, existing configurations and other components.

Add a normal native-CI regression matrix across stable/unstable kernels
and cgroup v1/v2. A sparse 256 GiB device exercises the large metadata
allocation without requiring bulk disk writes. Activate/deactivate it
twice, check usable capacity and an empty swap table after cleanup,
and reject kernel warning taint. Print the kernel log on setup failure.
Four independent instances use the existing parallel resource scheduler.

Validation: all four original-pin instances reproduce swapon ENOMEM.
Component allocation deltas pass checkpatch; Nix formatting, parsing and
native Overcommit pass. Canonical archive-byte hashes were prefetched,
and fleet retention checks pass before and after the pin edits. Local
source probes identify the repaired kernel derivations before boot.
Fixed runtime and normal feature-branch CI results gate promotion; they
are not claimed as passed by this commit. No deployment is performed.

tests/kernel: exercise proxy execution in normal CI

The general native suite selects the ci tag. Registering the proxy lock
contention test without that tag leaves the unstable scheduler path out
of ordinary qualification even though the product kernel enables it.

Add ci while retaining the existing proxy-exec tag, opt-in controls and
strict assertions. Default the proxy QEMU configuration to the maintained
unstable kernel: the general stable default does not carry proxy execution.
Explicit kernel-version, source-snapshot and staged-artifact development
paths remain available. Document the default independently of suite choice.

The existing native scheduler runs this case alongside independent tests;
this change adds no runner or campaign. The enabled-mode default is not
full lock-class or disabled-control qualification. It also does not claim
that the separate scheduler list corruption has been repaired.

Validation: native Overcommit passed. Before this correction, direct Nix
evaluation selected Linux 6.12.113 for the proxy fixture. The corrected
selection and actual CI results are recorded in the incident work log.
